unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U17: Classify incorporation and member-liability forms

payload.title: Use more than one classification axis
payload.core_explanation_md:
A statutory corporation derives its constitution and powers from its special law; a registered company is incorporated through the company-law framework. Check the special-law applicability provisions instead of assuming every statutory body follows every Companies Act provision identically.

Liability is a separate axis. In a company limited by shares, the member exposure is the unpaid amount on the shares under the described rule. A guarantee company has the undertaking to contribute on winding up; where it also has share capital, the relevant capital obligation is additional. An unlimited company cannot be analysed through a limited-by-shares shortcut. These categories concern member liability, not whether the entity must honour its own contracts.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a guarantee company necessarily have no share capital?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The source recognises both possibilities.
